messages:
Maria: We got ~20 pages for GPU node OOMs at 02:15 UTC during the nightly batch run. Woke oncall and looks like cascading failures.
Chris: Confirmed. Many pods hit cache pressure and kubelet triggered OOM. Pages were one-per-node -> flood.
Sam: Can you post the alert rule that fired?
Maria: Here it is:
```
- alert: gpu_node_oom
  expr: kube_node_status_condition{condition="OutOfMemory"} == 1
  for: 30s
  labels:
    severity: page
  annotations:
    summary: "OOM on {{ $labels.node }}"
```
Maria: It's severity=page and no grouping, so each node created a separate page.
Jing: That's too noisy for expected batch churn. Suggest single-node -> ticket; cluster-level cascades -> page.
Kevin: Proposal:
- single node OOM: severity=warning -> create ops ticket
- cluster cascade (>=3 nodes in 5m): severity=page
- add alert that counts recent OOM events and triggers at threshold
Chris: Proposed cluster alert:
```
- alert: gpu_oom_cluster_cascade
  expr: increase(gpu_node_oom_total[5m]) >= 3
  for: 2m
  labels:
    severity: page
```
Sam: For single-node tickets, ops-bot should attach recent kubelet logs and last 200 lines of gpu-manager log.
Maria: ops-bot: create-ticket template? (testing bot)
ops-bot: @Maria created ticket INF-5012 using template "node-oom-basic". Included kubelet and gpu-manager snippets.
Jing: Also recommend adding a label like page_when: cluster_wide to alerts that should be routed to pagerduty only when cluster-level.
Kevin: For alertmanager, we should add a mute route for cluster=batch-nightly between 02:00-04:30 UTC. We don't have cron silences in AM, so automation will create scheduled silences.
Chris: Note: don't mute critical control-plane nodes. Keep pages for masters and autoscaler nodes.
Sam: Let's add a fallback: if ticket count from same cluster > 5 in 30m, auto-promote to page.
Maria: Pseudo alertmanager route sketch:
```
routes:
- match:
    cluster: batch-nightly
  receiver: clustered-tickets
  continue: true
  mute_window: "02:00-04:30"
- match_re:
    severity: "page|critical"
  receiver: pagerduty
```
Maria: (we'll implement mute as scheduled silences via automation)
Kevin: Also add an SLO panel: "healthy GPU capacity" = healthy_gpu_nodes / total_gpu_nodes. Alert ticket when it drops <95% for >10m.
Jing: Good idea. That helps tie alerts to customer impact rather than raw node events.
Chris: I'll run a replay of last night's incidents against the new grouping rules to validate.
Maria: Action items:
- Update gpu_node_oom rule -> warning for single node (owner: Sam) due today
- Add gpu_oom_cluster_cascade (owner: Jing) due tomorrow AM
- Add scheduled-silence automation for batch-nightly (owner: Kevin) due this week
- Ops-bot ticket payload update (owner: Maria) due EOD
- Add SLO panel and alert (owner: Chris) due next week
Sam: I'll open the PR after making the rule change and include test queries and noise-replay results.
Maria: Thanks everyone. Please ack when you review the PR.
ops-bot: Scheduled silence created for cluster=batch-nightly from 02:00 to 04:30 UTC (ID: S-20260318-batch)
Chris: Acked. I'll kick off replay tomorrow and report findings.
Jing: Ack. Will write the cluster cascade rule and add test cases.
Kevin: Ack. Will wire up the silence automation to our ops scheduler.
Maria: Closing the loop: PR link will be posted in #eng-sre/alerting-review. :thumbsup:
